The structure is described in the rhombohedral space group R3m, number 160, with Hall symbol R 3 -2". The input lattice is specified by parameters a = 17.12150876 Å, b = 17.12150876 Å, c = 17.12150854 Å, α = 13.829244589999966°, β = 13.829244589999966°, and γ = 13.829246229999946°, and it contains ten atoms with the declared composition Zn₄Cd₁Se₅. Fractional coordinates are used throughout, and the supplied relation between the standard and input frames is q_standard = P q_input + s, where P has rows (0.6666666666666664, -0.33333333333333337, -0.3333333333333334), (0.3333333333333331, 0.3333333333333332, -0.6666666666666669), and (0.33333333333333337, 0.33333333333333337, 0.33333333333333337), and the origin shift s is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). The input coordinates were rounded to six digits before any correction, and in this case no positional corrections were applied.

All ten independent atomic positions lie on the threefold axis at the special Wyckoff position 3a with coordinate relation (0, 0, z), so the entire structure is generated by stacking atoms along the c direction with x = y = 0. There are four inequivalent zinc orbits, each of multiplicity three: Zn at z = 0.597345, Zn at z = 0.19922100000000004, Zn at z = 0.800743, and Zn at z = 0.40286199999999994. A single cadmium orbit, also of multiplicity three, is located at z = 0.998908. Five inequivalent selenium orbits complete the structure, each again of multiplicity three, with representative z coordinates 0.946388, 0.548404, 0.15013400000000002, 0.751843, and 0.354151. Thus the crystal consists of ten symmetry-equivalent atomic layers repeated by the R3m rhombohedral symmetry, with the sequence along c given by these ten independent z values and no additional free positional parameters.
